tier: BLACK FRIDAY SPECIAL 1 GB and 2.5 GB KVM VPS

free_tier.stated: no free tier; the page offers 1 GB at USD 12 a year and 2.5 GB at USD 22 a year

retention.stated: the disk persists while the term is paid; no deletion clock stated

egress.terms: 3 TB a month at 1 Gbit/s on the 1 GB tier, 4 TB on the 2.5 GB tier

interface_detail: root SSH, self-service control panel, one IPv4 plus a /64 IPv6 subnet
tooling: any SSH client; the console at console.hostodo.com is a Next.js app whose deploy route needs a signed-in session
chaining: USD 12 a year for 1 GiB with IPv6 would answer the WireGuard question, if the deploy route could be read without an account.

limits.value: 3 TB a month at 1 Gbit/s on the 1 GB tier

binding_note: The checkout, not the offer: the page is live, dated 2025 and priced, but console.hostodo.com renders client-side, so the price at checkout is unverified. The caveat is unreadability, not a known repricing.

identity_cost.detail: signup at console.hostodo.com is required before the order links work; the page lists 'Credit Card, PayPal, AliPay, and Crypto Accepted'. No hold stated.

confidence_note: The sale page was read and its prices are quoted. The cart was not readable, so the price at checkout is unverified rather than confirmed. The record's weakest field is the cart, which makes it unverified.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'BLACK FRIDAY SPECIAL 1GB RAM ... 20GB NVMe ... 3TB @ 1Gbit/s ... $12/year [ORDER NOW]'; '2.5GB RAM ... 40GB NVMe ... 4TB ... $22/year $38/2 years | $50/3 years'; the page reads 'LIMITED TIME OFFER - BLACK FRIDAY 2025'
HTTP 200, 2,006 bytes, sha256 ffc79d5dcba383e5... - a Next.js shell with an empty #__next div and no price in the bytes
control: HTTP 200, 2,006 bytes, sha256 ffc79d5dcba383e5... - byte-identical to the real plan code, which proves the route does not encode a product and the 200 is not evidence of an offer
redirects to /black-friday-2025, so the short path is the same page

notes: The sale page is live, dated 2025 and priced, and the order links are real console routes, but the console is a client-rendered app: the deploy URL returns the same 2,006 bytes for a valid plan code and a made-up one, so nothing about price or stock can be read without signing in. That control is the reason this row is unverified rather than a finding - without it the HTTP 200 would have looked like a working cart. Does not create accounts. The verdict is qualifies-with-caveat rather than dead because the page and its prices are first-party and current; it is not qualifies because nothing confirms the cart still charges them.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 12 a year divided by 12 is USD 1.00 a month, paid once. The 2.5 GB tier is USD 22 a year, USD 1.8333 a month; its two-year price of USD 38 is USD 1.5833 a month.
extras.locations: Detroit MI (DET01), Tampa FL (TPA01), Las Vegas NV (LAS01)
extras.price_on_page: USD 12.00/yr for 1 GB (page), USD 22.00/yr for 2.5 GB
extras.cart_note: the deploy URL resolves and renders a console, but no price line was readable in the server-rendered HTML; a control request with a bogus plan code returned byte-identical output, so the 200 establishes nothing about this plan
